- Option B: Wed, Jan 20 — 2:00–3:30 PM EST / 11:00–12:30 PM PST

Draft agenda (attached):
1) 10 min — kickoff & success criteria
2) 35 min — prompt review & hands-on prompt refinement
3) 25 min — routing discussion + configuration walkthrough
4) 20 min — lightweight load test run + interpret results

Attachments: blueridge_poc_agenda.pdf (agenda + checklist). We'll also bring an initial prompt set for you to try (initial_prompt_set.yaml). If you confirm a slot, I'll send a calendar invite and a short pre-work checklist for your engineering team (anything you want us to instrument or measure during the load test).

A couple of questions to help us prepare:
- Who on your side will own the load-test VM / endpoint access?
- Any constraints around installing a small load harness?

If neither slot works, share 2 convenient times and we'll adapt.

Best,

Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:37:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: POC working session: kickoff, prompt review & load-test plan — recap & next steps

Hi all — thanks for a productive session earlier today. Below is a short recap and concrete action items. Recording & artifacts are linked at the bottom.

Recap (high level):
- Prompt review: refined warm-start prompts, removed redundant system-level constraints that caused repetition. Priya flagged two prompts that needed role-based context; we added placeholders and test tokens.
- Routing: demoed model routing by intent; fallback to smaller quantized model on high latencies worked as expected.
- Load test: ran a 2-minute burst (10 concurrent threads). Observed p95 ~ 420ms on cold KV loads; p95 ~ 160ms with warm cache. No errors, but token throughput dropped with long context sizes (>1024).

Action items (owner — due):
- Sam (Blue Ridge): provide VM IP and test API key by Fri, Jan 22 EOD — required for expanded load runs.
- Dev (Redwood): extend the load harness to include long-context scenario and share script — due Mon, Jan 25.
- Evelyn (Redwood): produce trimmed prompt set and regression test cases (5 prompts) — due Mon, Jan 25.
- Aditya (Redwood): prepare pricing/throughput estimate for sustained 200 qps with caching — due Wed, Jan 27.

Notes / risks:
- Long-context throughput is the primary risk area. We recommend continuing with caching and considering quantized variants for tail traffic.

Next session: propose a follow-up technical deep-dive week of Jan 25–29 (60–90 minutes) focused on routing policies and expanded load runs. Priya — please confirm a preferred day/time and we'll circulate a calendar invite.

Artifacts:
- Session recording: [Attachment: session_recording_link.txt] (https://drive.google.com/file/d/recording123)
- Working prompts: initial_prompt_set.yaml (attached earlier)
- Load harness: link in shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1x2y3z_blueridge-poc

Thanks again — pleased with the progress. Looking forward to the next dive.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
